Hi — this is l3-gpu, the owner of P14 in the Vellum move program.

The change in this PR, linking wgpu-native only when the renderer has no Skia Dawn, is P14, which is **Pulp #10053** (https://github.com/Generous-Corp/pulp/pull/10053). 20 of the files here are identical to that PR.

The one real addition here is commit `9c63d585098b067ccd71162c3cf10e8657d5c555` ("test: keep renderer portability checks provider-aware"). It makes the Scene3D native-renderer link boundary accept Skia's static Dawn, and adds the installed `Pulp::render` staging fixture. It is now cherry-picked into #10053 with its original author and a `cherry picked from` trailer.
- Its `PulpRuntimeStaging.cmake` hunk was not taken, because #10053 already reads an installed `Pulp::render` through `INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES`.
- Checked locally on a Makefiles `-DPULP_ENABLE_SCENE3D=ON` configure:
  - the new boundary verifier reports `native_renderer_boundary_verified=7 link files`;
  - the negative contract reports `verified=true`;
  - the previous verifier fails on that configure with "missing required native WebGPU runtime token 'libwgpu_native'", which confirms the SCENE3D red was caused by P14.

So nothing unique is left in this PR. Could its author please close it? I'm not closing another session's PR myself. Thanks for finding the Scene3D fix.

## fable-graph review of 61758c76630e37ca28253dfe80cd69573a849e2e: HOLD (the check catches none of its replay set; four must-fix items)

**What holds.** The hook and `gates.sh` fetch `origin main` before anything else and run `tools/scripts/merge_tree_script_state.py` against `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`. The script never pushes and never writes a ref: it makes a dangling `commit-tree` object and a temporary detached worktree, then removes it (contract row 2 is respected; an armed or approved head is only read). Offline it fails closed (`exit 2`), which Appendix C accepted for the hook. A real conflict is refused with the "would be DIRTY" message and the focused suite covers that path: `test_refresh_push_check.py` 13/13 at this head. All six live required contexts are success on the exact head (`macos`, `Enforce version & skill sync`, `drift-fast`, `Vellum freeze`, `Vellum trusted freeze` as a commit status, `Build + prove + (owner-gated) deploy`); the head is behind main and needs a merge-only update regardless.

**Cost, measured:** 22 s wall (18 s user) against real `origin/main` in a worktree on m3, on top of the existing hook. Most of it is a full `git worktree add` of the tree plus the first check (see item 2), which can never fail here.

**Replay of the P0-1 set the plan names (section 12), run through the shipped script with base = the main sha encoded in each `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-<sha>` ref and head = the PR's last commit before the run; failing ctest names read from the six job logs:**

| Case | Ejecting test | Queue base | Shipped check result | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #8891 | `consumption-census-drift` (`--check --build-dir`) | 2c590498, on main (class i) | rc=1, **spurious**: the old tree's `vellum_watch_preflight.py` rejects `--enforce`; the control with the branch's own merge-base fails identically, so nothing was discriminated | the hook runs `consumption_census.py --validate-only` (schema only); `--check` reads a configured build dir |
| #8912 | same | e4272502, **not on main** (a queue-chain merge: class v) | same spurious rc=1 | same |
| #9177 | `sample-region-compat-baseline` (nested build, 70-270 s) | f7b52b96, on main | spurious rc=1 as above | compiled; out of hook scope per Appendix C(a)4 |
| #10053(b) | `vellum-inheritance-ledger` | 5fe754e5, **not on main** (= the queue merge of #10071, whose ledger script is on neither #10053's head nor current main: class v) | **rc=0, not caught** | the script's "vellum-inheritance-ledger" entry runs `vellum_watch_preflight.py --enforce`, which is the vellum-watch/freeze gate, not the ledger; the real check is `tools/scripts/vellum_inheritance_ledger_check.py`, and run directly on the materialized synthetic merge it reproduces job 114476562680 in 0.09 s (`docs/contracts/vellum-inheritance-ledger.md is frozen; record new entries as files under ...`) |
| #10084 (both runs) | `upgrade runtime list matches the canonical browser manifest` + `upgrade-installed browser runtime resolves its relative module graph` | e3c87022 (= #10053's own queue merge, not on main) and d9b895dc (on main) | **rc=0, not caught** | Catch2 `TEST_CASE`s in `test/test_cli_upgrade_install.cpp`: compiled, out of scope |

Net: 0 of 5 named cases are caught for the stated reason. Two of the five (and both #10084 bases but one) are class (v) batch-mate ejections, which Appendix C says R1 cannot prevent, so the plan's own replay table needs correcting; the catchable one (#10053's ledger) is missed because the wrong script is wired under its name. There is no positive test anywhere in the PR that a drifted manifest on the merge tree makes the check fail; the only tested behaviour is conflict refusal.

**Must-fix:**
1. `merge_tree_script_state.py`: the `vellum-inheritance-ledger` entry must run `tools/scripts/vellum_inheritance_ledger_check.py` (guarded by `.exists()`, since current main does not carry it), not `vellum_watch_preflight.py --enforce`; keep the watch-preflight under its own name if it is wanted.
2. `_run()` returns 0 whenever a failing run's output contains `NOT CHECKED locally:`. In the build-less temp worktree the first entry (`gates_script_inputs.py`) always prints that line, so it always returns 0 (observed on every run, including when it also printed `changed-surface script families: FAILED, not verified`); a static families flip in the same run would be masked too. Drop the first entry (the second entry already runs `changed_surface_script_families.py --static` directly) or make the mask apply only when that path alone produced the non-zero exit.
3. Honor the hook's documented knobs and base: the new fetch+check runs before `PULP_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` ("skip ALL gates entirely") and `PULP_DISABLE_PREPUSH_GATES=1`, with no demotion, and hard-codes `origin/main` while the hook's own `BASE` honours `PULP_PREPUSH_BASE` at line 277. A stacked branch, a `develop/*` branch, or an `explore/*` branch that legitimately conflicts with main is now unpushable, and the emergency skip no longer skips. Use `${PULP_PREPUSH_BASE:-origin/main}` and place the check after the skip (or demote with the knobs), as the refresh-push guard above it already does.
4. Make the coverage claim true and tested: the title says "complete merged-tree manifest coverage" and the plan says P0-1 catches #8891/#8912 in seconds; neither is so. State in `docs/guides`/the plan which classes the hook can see (`ctest_script_inputs.json` only with a configured build, families static, agent-capabilities, unregistered-tests, ledger when present) and which it cannot (census `--check`, sample-region, upgrade-runtime: all need a build), re-scope the replay set to class (i) cases the check can catch, and add one positive case to `test_refresh_push_check.py`: a synthetic repo where main moves a manifest input and the merge tree fails the check while the head alone passes.

**Should-fix-soon, not blocking:** (a) `gates.sh` now exits 2 offline even with a custom base, a regression for an on-demand runner that used to work offline; warn and continue with the stale-ref caveat there. (b) Cleanup is not robust: `git worktree list` on this host shows a leftover `agent-worktrees/pulp-merge-tree-175zzz21` whose HEAD is a `pulp-gates` "merge-tree script-state" commit from 13:09 -0700 today (the author's own run, before mine; my nine runs cleaned up). Add a `git worktree prune` and a signal-safe trap. (c) 22 s per push: materialize only the paths the six scripts read, or reuse one scratch worktree. (d) `.shipyard/changed-surface-families.toml` loses the whole `script-readers-4725620f7866` family and two aggregate entries for `tools/scripts/unregistered_tests_check.py`, a file this PR does not touch, so an edit to that script will select no tests; the drift check is diff-scoped, which is why CI did not ask. Explain or revert. (e) The check also runs for tag pushes and branch deletes.

No `reviewed:` line; this head is not approved. HOLD.

## fable-graph review of 257d63ed9edb8bfbdc97461fb6530545b87e02c9: APPROVED conditional on `macos` and a merge-only update from main

**Every must-fix from 61758c76 is addressed, verified by re-running my replay, not by reading the diff.**
1. Ledger: the check now runs `tools/scripts/vellum_inheritance_ledger_check.py --root <tree> --base <base>` when that script exists in the merge tree (the script on the #10053 queue-base tree accepts exactly `--root`/`--base`, so this is not a usage-error "catch"). Replay #10053 (base 5fe754e5, head 62652848): rc=1 with the genuine message `vellum-inheritance-ledger: docs/contracts/vellum-inheritance-ledger.md is frozen; record new entries as files under ...`, i.e. job 114476562680 reproduced build-free. Control with the branch's own merge-base (855dcbd3): rc=0. The instrument now discriminates.
2. Masking: `_run()` returns the child's exit code unconditionally; `case_script_failure_is_not_masked_by_not_checked` proves a failing child that prints `NOT CHECKED locally:` still fails. The always-vacuous `gates_script_inputs.py` entry is gone unless `PULP_GATES_BUILD_DIR` names a configured build, and the census schema validator is no longer passed off as the drift check: replay #8891 is rc=0 with `script-test-inputs-drift (no build-free variant; skipped)` printed, which is the truthful result (census `--check` needs a build). #10084b rc=0 likewise (compiled Catch2).
3. Hook knobs: the merge-tree check moved after the `PULP_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` exit (line 154 -> check at 162-170) and uses `${PULP_PREPUSH_BASE:-origin/main}`, so stacked branches compare against their declared base and the emergency skip skips it; `gates.sh` passes its own `$BASE`.
4. Coverage claim: the title/commits now say "build-free" and "scope merged-tree checks to build-free tools"; the test suite gained `case_ledger_checker_selected_from_merge_tree` (a synthetic repo where main adds a drifting ledger and the merge tree fails while `consumption-census-schema` is absent) and `case_merge_tree_conflict_refuses`. `test_refresh_push_check.py`: 15/15 at this head.

**Cost:** 19.2 s wall / 15.2 s user against real `origin/main` (was 22 s). Nine replay and control runs left no new `pulp-merge-tree-*` worktree; the one leftover on this host is still the author's 13:09 -0700 run.

**Live required contexts (6, strict), exact head:** `Enforce version & skill sync`, `drift-fast`, `Vellum freeze`, `Vellum trusted freeze` (commit status), `Build + prove + (owner-gated) deploy` success; `macos` queued. The head is 2 commits behind main; a merge-only update is needed before the queue takes it, and the `reviewed:` line follows the six contexts being success on the updated head.

**Should-fix-soon, not blocking (carried, with two new):**
- (a) The original top-of-hook `git fetch` (line 31-37) is still there, before `PULP_SKIP_PREPUSH`, and a second identical fetch now runs at line 163. Drop the first: it costs a round trip on every push and is the one path on which `PULP_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` still fails closed offline.
- (b) `PULP_DISABLE_PREPUSH_GATES=1` does not demote the merge-tree check, although the comment above it says it runs "only when the normal gates are enabled". Demote it with the others.
- (c) `explore/*` branches are expected to diverge and are never merged to main, yet a conflicting one is now unpushable without `PULP_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`. The hook reads the pushed refs from stdin; skip the check for `refs/heads/explore/*`.
- (d) `gates.sh` still exits 2 offline even with a custom base; warn and continue there.
- (e) `.shipyard/changed-surface-families.toml` still drops the `script-readers-4725620f7866` family and two aggregate entries for `tools/scripts/unregistered_tests_check.py`, a file this PR does not touch (now one the hook itself runs). The drift check is diff-scoped so CI will not ask; explain or revert.
- (f) Cleanup still lacks a signal-safe trap / `git worktree prune`; the leftover from the author's own run shows the failure mode.
- (g) Plan `section 12` should be corrected: #8912, #10053 and #10084a have queue bases that are not on main (batch-mate class), and the census/sample-region/upgrade-runtime cases need a build and are not P0-1 cases.

No `reviewed:` line yet; it follows `macos` and the merge-only update.
